catalog_quote: Languages of Sumba have vowel epenthesis (a.k.a. paragoge). Certain words with a final consonant undergo epenthesis in order to create a final open syllable. The epenthetic vowel is extra-metrical and does not shift stress from the penultimate vowel of the root. In Kambera the epenthetic vowel is [u]. Examples include: *quzan > uraŋ → uraŋ-u ‘rain’, *tasik > tehik → tehik-u ‘sea’, and *umpu > umbuk → umbuk-u ‘grandchild’ (Klamer 1998a: 19). In Weyewa, Loli, and Mamboru the epenthetic vowel is usually [a] (though exceptions occur); as in Weyewa tazik-a ‘sea’ and Mamboru umbuk-a ‘grandchild’. In Kodi the epenthetic vowel is [o].

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress falls on the penultimate vowel of the root; the paragogic final vowel (Mamboru -a, e.g. umbuk-a) is extrametrical and does not count, so such words surface with antepenultimate stress. This is a family-level generalisation over the languages of Sumba in a comparative handbook, applied to Mamboru by name; it is not drawn from a first-hand description of Mamboru (none exists). Consistent supporting evidence: Wielenga 1910 (Sumbanese from Kambera, with Memboro dialect notes) 'als een regel valt de klemtoon op de voorlaatste lettergreep.. De facultatieve sluit oe telt niet als lettergreep', and Wielenga 1917's dialect survey flags only Lamboja and Kodi as deviating in klemtoon, not Memboro.
new_statements.exceptions: Only that the quality of the Mamboru epenthetic vowel has exceptions ('usually [a] (though exceptions occur)'); no stress exceptions given for Mamboru.
new_statements.domain_note: Root/word level; paragogic vowel excluded from the count. Mamboru forms in this source are taken from Onvlee 1984 (dictionary data collected 1920-1950).
new_statements.identity_note: All sources refer to the same variety: Mamboru/Memboro/Mamboro [mvd], mamb1305, kecamatan Mamboru, north coast of central Sumba (ABVD list from desa Wendewa Selatan, with Cendana variants). Grimes & Edwards 2026 class it as the non-denasalising member of 'Central Sumba' (*s = s); Glottolog 5.1 places it in a 'Kambera' node with Kambera (kamb1299). The Wielenga 1910 klemtoon rule is explicitly for the Kambera dialect (kamb1299), not Mamboru.

sources.note: Generic Sumba statement naming Mamboru: the paragogic (epenthetic) final vowel is extra-metrical and 'does not shift stress from the penultimate vowel of the root'; in Weyewa, Loli and Mamboru the epenthetic vowel is usually [a] (Mamboru umbuk-a 'grandchild'). Comparative generalisation; their Mamboru data are from Onvlee 1984; no Mamboru-specific stress description cited.
